title: Survival Tower II: Proving Ground
subject: Science: Natural Selection (follow-up check)
intro: New animals, same rules. Moths, rabbits, bacteria and finches: prove you can use natural selection, not just remember the sheet.

questions.q: In biology, 'fitness' means surviving AND being able to ______.
questions.explain: Fitness is about passing on genes: an animal that lives a long time but never has offspring has low fitness.

questions.q: Which deer has the HIGHEST fitness?
choices: A small deer that lives 6 years and has 8 fawns
A huge, strong deer that lives 12 years and has no fawns
The fastest deer, which has 1 fawn
A deer that wins every fight but has 2 fawns
questions.explain: Fitness counts offspring, not size or strength. The deer with 8 fawns passes on the most genes.
questions.review: Fitness = survive AND reproduce (count the babies)

questions.q: A population of plants are all exact clones. A new disease arrives. Why is this dangerous for them?
choices: With no genetic variation, none may have a trait that resists the disease
questions.explain: Natural selection needs genetic variation. If every plant is identical, they all share the same weakness.

questions.q: Natural selection can only work if there is ______ variation (differences in the DNA) in the population.
questions.explain: Only genetic differences are inherited, so only genetic variation lets a population change over generations.

questions.q: A dog learns to open doors. Will her puppies be born knowing how?
choices: No, learned skills are not in the DNA
Yes, all skills are passed on
Only if she practices a lot
questions.explain: Learned behaviors and injuries are not genetic, so they are not inherited.

questions.q: A bacterium's DNA changes by accident when it copies itself, giving it a brand new trait. This change is called a ______.
questions.explain: A mutation is a change in DNA during copying. It is how brand-new traits appear.

questions.q: Where do brand-new traits, not found in either parent, come from?
questions.explain: Mixing parents' genes only reshuffles traits that already exist. Totally new traits come from mutations.

questions.q: Fish A reproduces sexually. Fish B reproduces asexually. Which species can adapt faster to a warming lake?
choices: Fish A, because sexual reproduction creates more variation
Fish B, because it makes copies faster
questions.explain: Sexual reproduction mixes two parents' genes, so the offspring vary more. More variation gives natural selection more to choose from, so evolution is faster.
questions.review: Sexual reproduction = more variation = FASTER evolution

questions.q: Because it makes more variation, evolution happens ______ in organisms that reproduce sexually. (faster or slower?)
questions.explain: More variation means more chances that some offspring have a helpful trait, so the population changes faster.

questions.q: Why do brothers and sisters look different from each other?
choices: Each gets a different mix of genes from the two parents
questions.explain: Sexual reproduction gives each child its own mix of the parents' genes.

questions.q: What is the FIRST step of natural selection?
questions.explain: Step 1 variation, step 2 the better-suited survive and reproduce more, step 3 their trait becomes common over generations.

questions.q: Put these in order: (1) more brown rabbits survive winter, (2) some rabbits are brown and some white, (3) most rabbits are now brown.
questions.explain: First variation exists (2), then the better-suited survive and reproduce (1), then the trait becomes common (3).

questions.q: Over 100 years a moth population changes from mostly light to mostly dark. What changed?
choices: The population: more dark moths survived and reproduced
The moths decided to be dark
One moth changed and the rest copied
questions.explain: Individuals cannot change their genes. The POPULATION changes because the better-suited ones leave more offspring.
questions.review: Natural selection changes POPULATIONS, not individuals

questions.q: Natural selection changes ______, not individuals.
questions.explain: A single animal keeps the genes it was born with; the mix of genes in the population is what shifts.

questions.q: Giraffes have long necks. Which explanation is correct?
choices: Giraffes born with longer necks reached more food, survived and had more babies
Giraffes stretched their necks and passed on the stretch
Short-necked giraffes grew taller each year
questions.explain: Stretching is not inherited. Giraffes BORN with longer necks did better and passed on long-neck genes over many generations.

questions.q: Natural selection is slow. It happens over many ______.
questions.explain: Each generation shifts the population a little, so big changes take many generations.

questions.q: Why do bacteria evolve antibiotic resistance in months, but elephants take thousands of years to change?
choices: Bacteria have a new generation every hour or so
questions.explain: Change happens per generation. Bacteria pack thousands of generations into a year.

questions.q: White and brown rabbits live in a snowy forest. Which ones will owls most likely see?
questions.explain: Brown stands out against white snow; white rabbits are camouflaged.
questions.review: The color that does NOT match the background gets seen and eaten

questions.q: On a beach of mostly dark gray rocks, which crabs survive best?
questions.explain: Crabs that match the background are hidden from birds, so they survive and reproduce more.

questions.q: Bright red, blue and brown beetles live on brown tree bark. After many generations, most beetles will probably be...
questions.explain: Red and blue beetles are spotted and eaten; brown beetles survive and pass on brown genes.

questions.q: A drought means only hard seeds are left on an island. Finches with thick beaks can crack them. What happens to the next generations?
questions.explain: Thick-beaked finches eat, survive and reproduce more, so thick beaks become more common.

questions.q: A farmer sprays insect poison. A few bugs survive because of a mutation. Years later, the poison barely works. Why?
choices: The survivors passed on the resistance gene, so the population became resistant
The bugs got used to it during their lives
The bugs learned to hold their breath
questions.explain: Variation (the mutation) + selection (the poison kills the others) + inheritance over generations = a resistant population.
